win98.help.agriculture_animal_type: Sets which kind of animal this pasture keeps. Apply the new type before you set its population limits and foods.
win98.help.agriculture_animals: Lists the animals in this pasture with their sex and age. Check an animal to have it butchered; it takes effect when you click Apply or OK.
win98.help.agriculture_farm_catalog: Lists the crops or trees you know, with seeds on hand, the number planted and the number stored. Click one to make it the default crop or the grove's tree type; it takes effect when you click Apply or OK.
win98.help.agriculture_female_cap: Sets how many females of this pasture's animal type may be assigned to it. Use the limits to control breeding and keep room in the pasture.
win98.help.agriculture_foods: Lists the foods known for this pasture's animal type. Check the foods the animals may eat; changes take effect when you click Apply or OK.
win98.help.agriculture_harvest: Shows whether gnomes harvest here. For a grove, it shows whether they pick fruit.
win98.help.agriculture_locate: Click this to center the map view on this area.
win98.help.agriculture_male_cap: Sets how many males of this pasture's animal type may be assigned to it. Use the limits to control breeding and keep room in the pasture.
win98.help.agriculture_name: Sets the name of this farm, grove or pasture. The change takes effect when you click Apply or OK.
win98.help.agriculture_order_down: Click this to move the selected planting one place lower, so it is planted later.
win98.help.agriculture_order_remove: Click this to remove the selected planting from the plot's queue.
win98.help.agriculture_order_up: Click this to move the selected planting one place higher, so it is planted sooner.
win98.help.agriculture_planted: Shows how many plots are planted.
win98.help.agriculture_plot_assign: Click this to make the selected plots always grow the chosen crop. It takes effect right away.
win98.help.agriculture_plot_clear: Click this to clear the plot selection.
win98.help.agriculture_plot_count: Sets how many plantings of the chosen crop the Queue button adds to each selected plot.
win98.help.agriculture_plot_crop: Sets the crop used by the Assign, Queue and Queue Repeat buttons for the selected plots.
win98.help.agriculture_plot_default: Click this to remove the assigned crop from the selected plots, so they grow the farm's default crop again.
win98.help.agriculture_plot_grid: Shows each plot on this farm and whether it is untilled, tilled or ready; a faded icon shows the crop planned for it. Click a plot to select it, Ctrl+click to add or remove one, or Shift+click to select a rectangle.
win98.help.agriculture_plot_orders: Lists the plantings queued on the selected plot; they are planted from top to bottom. Click a planting to move or remove it.
win98.help.agriculture_plot_queue: Click this to add plantings of the chosen crop to the queue of each selected plot. Queued plantings are grown before the plot's assigned crop.
win98.help.agriculture_plot_repeat: Click this to add a repeating planting of the chosen crop to each selected plot. It keeps coming back, moving behind later plantings each time it is planted.
win98.help.agriculture_plot_select_all: Click this to select every plot on this farm, so the commands below change them all.
win98.help.agriculture_plots: Shows how many plots this farm, pasture or grove has.
win98.help.agriculture_priority: Shows the priority of this farm, pasture or grove. Gnomes work higher-priority ones first.
win98.help.agriculture_product: Shows what this farm, pasture or grove produces.
win98.help.agriculture_ready: Shows how many plots are ready to harvest.
win98.help.agriculture_state: Shows whether this farm, pasture or grove is being worked or is suspended.
win98.help.agriculture_toggle_fell: Sets whether gnomes cut down the trees in this grove for wood. The trees are removed.
win98.help.agriculture_toggle_harvest: Sets whether gnomes harvest crops on this farm when they are ripe.
win98.help.agriculture_toggle_hay: Sets whether gnomes cut hay from the grass in this pasture, to feed animals.
win98.help.agriculture_toggle_pasture_ha: Sets whether gnomes collect products from the animals in this pasture.
win98.help.agriculture_toggle_pick: Sets whether gnomes pick fruit from the trees in this grove.
win98.help.agriculture_toggle_plant: Sets whether gnomes plant trees in this grove.
win98.help.agriculture_toggle_primary: Click this to turn harvesting on or off. For a grove, it turns fruit picking on or off.
win98.help.agriculture_toggle_suspended: Stops all work in this area while checked. Clear the check box to let gnomes work here again.
win98.help.agriculture_toggle_tame: Marks this pasture as wanting wild animals tamed. The setting is saved with the pasture.
win98.help.agriculture_view_animals: Shows the Animals page, where you choose the pasture's animal type, set population limits and mark animals to butcher.
win98.help.agriculture_view_crops: Shows the page where you choose the farm's default crop, or the type of tree this grove grows.
win98.help.agriculture_view_food: Shows the Food page, where you choose which foods the pasture's animals may eat.
win98.help.agriculture_view_general: Shows the General page, where you rename this area, choose which work is done and see its status.
win98.help.agriculture_view_plots: Shows the Plots page, where you choose farm plots and set the crop each one grows.
win98.help.agriculture_view_queue: Shows the Plot Queue page, which lists the plantings waiting on the one selected plot.
win98.help.attitude_attack: Makes the squad fight this target when it is in sight and within reach. Choosing a response does not start an attack.
win98.help.attitude_defend: Makes the squad fight this target only when it comes very close. Choosing a response does not start an attack.
win98.help.attitude_flee: Makes the squad avoid fighting this target. Choosing a response does not start an attack.
win98.help.attitude_hunt: Makes the squad seek out this target anywhere it can reach, which is useful for clearing dangerous creatures. Choosing a response does not start an attack.
win98.help.blueprint_cancel_job: Click this to cancel the construction and remove the blueprint from the map.
win98.help.blueprint_lower_job: Click this to lower the priority of this construction job, so gnomes do other work first.
win98.help.blueprint_missing_items: Lists the materials this construction still needs, and how many of each. Gnomes cannot build it until the materials are available, so make or gather them.
win98.help.blueprint_priority: Shows the priority of this construction job. Gnomes do higher-priority jobs first.
win98.help.blueprint_raise_job: Click this to raise the priority of this construction job, so gnomes build it sooner.
win98.help.blueprint_skill: Shows the skill a gnome needs to build this. Only a gnome with this skill active can take the job.
win98.help.blueprint_tool: Shows the tool needed to build this and whether one is available.
win98.help.blueprint_worker: Shows the gnome assigned to build this, or Unassigned if no gnome has taken the job yet.
win98.help.common.apply: Saves the changes you have made without closing this window.
win98.help.common.cancel: Closes this window without saving any changes you have made.
win98.help.common.caption_help: Click this, and then click an item in the window to learn what it is and why you would use it.
win98.help.common.ok: Closes this window and saves any changes you have made.
win98.help.confirm-accept: Click this to carry out the action this message asks about.
win98.help.confirm-alternate: Click this to choose the other answer named on the button, as the message describes.
win98.help.confirm-cancel: Click this to close the message without carrying out the action. Nothing changes.
win98.help.creature_equipment_slot_arms: Shows the arm armor slot. For a citizen with a military role, click it to change the arm armor of that role's uniform.
win98.help.creature_equipment_slot_back: Shows what is worn on the back. For a citizen with a military role, click it to change what the role's uniform puts there.
win98.help.creature_equipment_slot_chest: Shows the chest armor slot. For a citizen with a military role, click it to change the chest armor of that role's uniform.
win98.help.creature_equipment_slot_feet: Shows the foot armor slot. For a citizen with a military role, click it to change the foot armor of that role's uniform.
win98.help.creature_equipment_slot_hands: Shows the hand armor slot. For a citizen with a military role, click it to change the hand armor of that role's uniform.
win98.help.creature_equipment_slot_head: Shows the head armor slot. For a citizen with a military role, click it to change the head armor of that role's uniform.
win98.help.creature_equipment_slot_left_: Shows what is held in the left hand. For a citizen with a military role, click it to change what the role's uniform holds there.
win98.help.creature_equipment_slot_legs: Shows the leg armor slot. For a citizen with a military role, click it to change the leg armor of that role's uniform.
win98.help.creature_equipment_slot_right: Shows what is held in the right hand. For a citizen with a military role, click it to change what the role's uniform holds there.
win98.help.creature_preview_activity: Shows what the creature is doing right now.
win98.help.creature_preview_camera_image: Shows a view of the selected creature in the world.
win98.help.creature_preview_camera_posit: Shows where the creature is on the map.
win98.help.creature_preview_charisma: Shows the creature's Charisma. Attributes are set from 1 to 10 when the creature is created.
win98.help.creature_preview_constitution: Shows the creature's Constitution. Attributes are set from 1 to 10 when the creature is created.
win98.help.creature_preview_dexterity: Shows the creature's Dexterity. Attributes are set from 1 to 10 when the creature is created.
win98.help.creature_preview_equipment: Lists each equipment slot and the item in it. For a citizen with a military role, click a slot to change that part of the role's uniform.
win98.help.creature_preview_equipment_ma: Sets the material the item in this slot must be made of. Choose Any to accept any material, so the item is easier to find.
win98.help.creature_preview_equipment_ty: Sets the kind of item this uniform slot should hold. Choose Empty to leave the slot bare. The change is made when you click Apply, for every citizen with this role.
win98.help.creature_preview_happiness: Shows how happy the creature is, from 0 to 100, where 100 means fully content.
win98.help.creature_preview_hunger: Shows how well fed the creature is, from 0 to 100, where 100 means fully met. A low value means it needs food soon.
win98.help.creature_preview_intelligence: Shows the creature's Intelligence. Attributes are set from 1 to 10 when the creature is created.
win98.help.creature_preview_inventory: Lists the items the creature is carrying right now.
win98.help.creature_preview_locate: Click this to move the map view so the creature is in the middle of the screen.
win98.help.creature_preview_nav_camera: Shows a view of the creature, what it is doing and where it is.
win98.help.creature_preview_nav_equipmen: Shows what the creature wears and holds in each slot, and lets you change the uniform of a citizen's military role.
win98.help.creature_preview_nav_expertis: Shows the citizen's profession and skills, and lets you change the profession.
win98.help.creature_preview_nav_inventor: Shows the items the creature is carrying.
win98.help.creature_preview_nav_stats: Shows the creature's attributes and how well its needs are met.
win98.help.creature_preview_profession: Sets this citizen's profession. The change takes effect at once. The profession decides which skills are active, and so which kinds of work the citizen does.
win98.help.creature_preview_skill_sort_a: Click this to list active skills first, so you can see which kinds of work the citizen does now.
win98.help.creature_preview_skill_sort_l: Click this to sort the skills by level, highest first, so you can see what the citizen is best at.
win98.help.creature_preview_skill_sort_n: Click this to sort the skills by name.
win98.help.creature_preview_skills: Lists the citizen's skills, the level of each and whether it is active. The citizen does only work that uses an active skill; change the profession to change which skills are active.
win98.help.creature_preview_skills_scrol: Lists the citizen's skills, the level of each and whether it is active. The citizen does only work that uses an active skill; change the profession to change which skills are active.
win98.help.creature_preview_sleep: Shows how rested the creature is, from 0 to 100, where 100 means fully rested. A low value means it needs sleep soon.
win98.help.creature_preview_strength: Shows the creature's Strength. Attributes are set from 1 to 10 when the creature is created; Strength adds to the damage it does in a fight.
win98.help.creature_preview_thirst: Shows how much the creature has had to drink, from 0 to 100, where 100 means fully met. A low value means it needs a drink soon.
win98.help.creature_preview_wisdom: Shows the creature's Wisdom. Attributes are set from 1 to 10 when the creature is created.
win98.help.diplomacy_error_retry: Click this to load the neighbor and mission lists again after they could not be loaded.
win98.help.diplomacy_gnome_rows: Lists the citizens who can go on this mission now. Click the citizen you want to send; they leave the settlement until the mission returns.
win98.help.diplomacy_mission_rows: Lists the missions your settlement has sent, with each mission's destination and status. Click a mission to see its task, citizens, time and result below.
win98.help.diplomacy_neighbor_rows: Lists the neighboring kingdoms your settlement knows about. Click a kingdom to see its details and to send a mission to it. Kingdoms not yet discovered show no details.
win98.help.diplomacy_tab_missions: Shows every mission your settlement has sent, where it went, and how it is going or how it ended.
win98.help.diplomacy_tab_neighbors: Shows the kingdoms your settlement knows about and the facts you have learned about each one. Choose a kingdom here before you send a mission to it.
win98.help.frame_close: Closes Ingnomia. Save your kingdom first if you want to keep your progress.
win98.help.frame_maximize: Enlarges the game window to fill the screen, or returns it to its previous size.
win98.help.frame_minimize: Hides the game window. Click its button on the taskbar to show it again.
win98.help.hud_active_tool: Shows the name of the tool you are using. Click or drag on the map to use it; right-click cancels it.
win98.help.hud_animals: Shows how many animals your settlement has.
win98.help.hud_build_containers: Lists the containers you can build in the item list. Containers hold stored items.
win98.help.hud_build_details: Shows the chosen item's materials. Use each drop-down to pick which material to use. Click Build, or Place Blueprint if items are missing, then click on the map to place it; a blueprint waits until the materials exist.
win98.help.hud_build_fence: Lists the fences you can build in the item list.
win98.help.hud_build_floor: Lists the floors you can build in the item list.
win98.help.hud_build_furniture: Lists the furniture you can build, such as beds and tables, in the item list.
win98.help.hud_build_items: Lists the items in the chosen category. Status shows Ready when you have the materials, or Needs items when they are missing. Click an item to see its materials and commands below.
win98.help.hud_build_ramps: Lists the ramps you can build in the item list. Ramps connect one level to another.
win98.help.hud_build_stairs: Lists the stairs you can build in the item list. Stairs connect one level to another.
win98.help.hud_build_type_list: Sets which kind of material the item list shows, such as wood, stone or metal. It appears when the chosen category has more than one kind.
win98.help.hud_build_type_select: Sets which kind of material the item list shows, such as wood, stone or metal. It appears when the chosen category has more than one kind.
win98.help.hud_build_utility: Lists the utility constructions you can build in the item list.
win98.help.hud_build_wall: Lists the walls you can build in the item list.
win98.help.hud_build_workshop: Lists the workshops you can build in the item list. Workshops are where your gnomes craft goods.
win98.help.hud_clock: Shows the time of day in the game.
win98.help.hud_date: Shows the current day and year in the game.
win98.help.hud_daylight: Shows whether it is day or night.
win98.help.hud_event_no: Click this to answer no to the event.
win98.help.hud_event_yes: Click this to answer yes to the event.
win98.help.hud_gnomes: Shows how many gnomes live in your settlement.
win98.help.hud_items: Shows how many items your settlement has.
win98.help.hud_kingdom: Shows the name of your kingdom.
win98.help.hud_level: Shows the map level you are looking at. Use Level Up and Level Down to change it.
win98.help.hud_level_down: Shows the map level below the current one. Use it to see and give orders underground, such as in mines. It is unavailable at the lowest level.
win98.help.hud_level_up: Shows the map level above the current one. Use it to return toward the surface or see upper floors. It is unavailable at the highest level.
win98.help.hud_mine_explorative: Selects the tool for marking an area for exploratory mining. Use it to search the rock for useful materials.
win98.help.hud_mine_hole: Selects the tool for digging a hole through the floor you mark. Use it to make an opening down to the level below.
win98.help.hud_mine_ramp_down: Selects the tool for digging a ramp leading down. Ramps connect a level to the one below.
win98.help.hud_mine_remove_floor: Selects the tool for removing the floor from the area you mark. Use it to open the ground to the level below.
win98.help.hud_mine_stairs_down: Selects the tool for digging stairs leading down. Stairs let your gnomes reach and work on the level below.
win98.help.hud_mine_stairs_up: Selects the tool for mining stairs leading up. Use it to give your gnomes a way to the level above.
win98.help.hud_mine_walls: Selects the tool for marking walls to be mined. Click or drag on the map; your gnomes dig out the marked walls, making room and producing stone.
win98.help.hud_open_diplomacy: Opens the Missions window, which shows neighboring kingdoms and missions. Use it to deal with the world beyond your settlement.
win98.help.hud_open_inventory: Opens the Inventory window, which lists the items your settlement has stored. Check it to see what materials you have before you build or craft.
win98.help.hud_open_military: Opens the Military window, where you set up squads, roles, uniforms and target priorities to defend your settlement.
win98.help.hud_open_population: Opens the Population window, which shows your citizens, their skills, professions and schedules. Use it to decide who does which kind of work.
win98.help.hud_overlay_axles: Shows powered mechanical axles on the map. A check mark means the setting is on. Use it to check how power reaches your machines.
win98.help.hud_overlay_designations: Shows or hides the designation markers on the map. A check mark means they are shown. Turn them on to see where your stockpiles, farms and rooms are.
win98.help.hud_overlay_jobs: Shows or hides the job markers on the map. A check mark means they are shown. Turn them on to see where work is waiting.
win98.help.hud_overlay_walls: Shows walls lowered for easier map viewing. A check mark means the setting is on. Use it to see into rooms and tunnels that walls would hide.
win98.help.hud_pause: Stops or restarts the game clock. Pause while you look around, plan orders or read a message; your gnomes do nothing until you resume.
win98.help.hud_size_grip: Drag this to change the size of the game window.
win98.help.hud_speed_fast: Runs the game at fast speed. Use it to pass quiet stretches, such as waiting for crops to grow or jobs to finish.
win98.help.hud_speed_normal: Runs the game at normal speed. Use it when you want to watch your gnomes closely or when things are busy.
win98.help.hud_status: Shows what the control under the pointer does, how to use the active tool, or a message about your last command. Read it when a command did not work.
win98.help.hud_tool_agriculture: Shows the tree and plant orders, such as cutting trees and foraging. Use them to gather wood, food and other plant materials.
win98.help.hud_tool_build: Opens the Build window, where you choose constructions, furniture and workshops to place on the map. Your gnomes then build them when the materials are available.
win98.help.hud_tool_cancel: Click this to stop using the current tool and return to inspecting the map. It is unavailable when no tool is active.
win98.help.hud_tool_cancel_job: Selects the tool for cancelling the job you click. Use it to remove an order you no longer want.
win98.help.hud_tool_deconstruct: Selects the Deconstruct tool. Click a constructed object on the map to have your gnomes take it down, for example to remove something placed in the wrong spot.
win98.help.hud_tool_designations: Shows the area designations, such as stockpiles, farms and rooms. Designations tell your gnomes what each area of the map is for.
win98.help.hud_tool_dining_hall: Selects the tool for designating an area where your gnomes eat.
win98.help.hud_tool_dormitory: Selects the tool for designating a shared sleeping area. Your gnomes need somewhere to sleep.
win98.help.hud_tool_farm: Selects the tool for designating an area for growing crops. Farms give your settlement a steady supply of food.
win98.help.hud_tool_fell_tree: Selects the tool for marking trees to be cut down. Cutting trees is the main way to get wood.
win98.help.hud_tool_forage: Selects the tool for gathering food and materials from wild plants in the area you mark. Foraging is useful for early food.
win98.help.hud_tool_forbidden: Selects the tool for designating an area your gnomes may not enter. Use it to keep them away from danger.
win98.help.hud_tool_grove: Selects the tool for designating an area for growing and harvesting trees.
win98.help.hud_tool_harvest_tree: Selects the tool for marking trees to harvest their products, such as fruit, without cutting them down.
win98.help.hud_tool_hospital: Selects the tool for designating an area for medical care of injured gnomes.
win98.help.hud_tool_inspect: Cancels the current tool so you can inspect the tile you click on the map. Use it to find out what is on a tile, such as a gnome, an item or a construction.
win98.help.hud_tool_jobs: Shows the job commands, which let you suspend, resume, cancel or reprioritize jobs you have already ordered.
win98.help.hud_tool_lower_priority: Selects the tool for moving the job you click lower in the work queue, so more urgent work is done first.
win98.help.hud_tool_mine: Shows the mining orders, such as mining walls or digging stairs. Mining clears space for your settlement and produces stone and ore.
win98.help.hud_tool_pasture: Selects the tool for designating an area for keeping animals.
win98.help.hud_tool_personal_room: Selects the tool for designating a room for one resident.
win98.help.hud_tool_plant_tree: Selects the tool for marking an area where trees will be planted. Plant trees to keep a supply of wood.
win98.help.hud_tool_raise_priority: Selects the tool for moving the job you click higher in the work queue, so your gnomes do it sooner.
win98.help.hud_tool_remove_designation: Selects the tool for clearing an existing area designation from the area you mark.
win98.help.hud_tool_remove_plant: Selects the tool for removing plants from the area you mark. Use it to clear ground for building or farming.
win98.help.hud_tool_resume_job: Selects the tool for resuming the suspended job you click, so your gnomes can work on it again.
win98.help.hud_tool_rotate: Turns the object you are placing a quarter turn. It is available only while the current tool places something that can turn, such as furniture.
win98.help.hud_tool_stockpile: Selects the tool for designating an area where items are stored. Stockpiles keep materials tidy and close to where they are needed.
win98.help.hud_tool_suspend_job: Selects the tool for pausing the job you click without removing it. Use it to hold work you want done later.
win98.help.hud_tool_view: Shows the View menu, where you show or hide map overlays such as designations and job markers.
win98.help.hud_watch_rows: Shows the counts of the items on your inventory watch list. Click a count to open the Inventory window.
win98.help.hud_whats_this: Click this, and then click an item in the game window to learn what it is and why you would use it.
win98.help.inspector_back: Click this to go back to what you were inspecting before this creature.
win98.help.inspector_locate: Click this to move the map view so the inspected object is in the middle of the screen.
win98.help.inspector_refresh: Click this to read the inspected object's details from the game again, so the values shown are up to date.
win98.help.inspector_root.agriculture_to: Click this to suspend work on this farm, pasture or grove, or to resume it. Suspending frees gnomes for other work.
win98.help.inspector_root.stockpile_prio: Shows this stockpile's priority. Gnomes fill higher-priority stockpiles first.
win98.help.inspector_root.stockpile_togg: Click this to suspend the stockpile so gnomes stop bringing items to it, or to resume it.
win98.help.inspector_root.workshop_prior: Shows this workshop's priority among your workshops. Gnomes work at higher-priority workshops first.
win98.help.inspector_root.workshop_produ: Shows how many different products this workshop can make.
win98.help.inspector_root.workshop_toggl: Click this to suspend the workshop so it takes no new jobs, or to resume work. Suspending frees gnomes for other work.
win98.help.inventory_category: Shows only items in the category you choose. Choose (All) to see every category.
win98.help.inventory_detail_equipped: Shows how many of this item are being worn or carried as equipment by creatures.
win98.help.inventory_detail_history: Lists the settlement's count of this item at the end of each day, with how many were made and how many were used that day. Use it to see whether your supply is growing or shrinking.
win98.help.inventory_detail_jobs: Shows how many of this item are claimed by jobs right now and so are not free for other work.
win98.help.inventory_detail_locations: Lists the stockpiles that hold this item and how many each one has. Click a stockpile, then click Properties to open it.
win98.help.inventory_detail_loose: Shows how many of this item are lying on the ground outside stockpiles. Loose items may need hauling.
win98.help.inventory_detail_made_by: Lists the workshops that make this item, how many each recipe makes, what it uses and the skill it needs.
win98.help.inventory_detail_open_product: Click this to see the properties of the item selected in the Used to make list.
win98.help.inventory_detail_open_stockpi: Click this to open the properties of the stockpile selected in the list.
win98.help.inventory_detail_stock: Shows how many of this item are stored in stockpiles.
win98.help.inventory_detail_tab_general: Shows where this item's count comes from, and lets you watch the item.
win98.help.inventory_detail_tab_history: Shows how the settlement's count of this item has changed from day to day.
win98.help.inventory_detail_tab_recipes: Shows which workshops make this item, from what, and what can be made from it.
win98.help.inventory_detail_tab_stockpil: Shows which stockpiles hold this item and how many each one has.
win98.help.inventory_detail_total: Shows how many of this item the settlement has in all, wherever they are.
win98.help.inventory_detail_used_in: Lists the items that can be made from this item. Click one, then click Properties to see that item.
win98.help.inventory_detail_watch: Adds this item to the watch list on the game screen, so you can follow its count while you play. Clear the check box to stop watching it.
win98.help.inventory_open_item: Click this to see the properties of the selected item, such as where it is stored, how it is made and how its count has changed.
win98.help.inventory_owned_only: Hides items the settlement has none of, so the list shows only what you actually own.
win98.help.inventory_rows: Lists your settlement's items, with how many are in stockpiles and how many there are in all. Check an item's box to watch it on the game screen; double-click an item to see its properties.
win98.help.inventory_search: Shows only items whose name, material, group or category contains the text you type. Use it to find an item quickly in a long list.
win98.help.inventory_sort_item: Click this to sort the list by item name. Click it again to reverse the order.
win98.help.inventory_sort_material: Click this to sort the list by material. Click it again to reverse the order.
win98.help.inventory_sort_stock: Click this to sort the list by how many are in stockpiles, largest first. Click it again to reverse the order.
win98.help.inventory_sort_total: Click this to sort the list by how many the settlement has in all, largest first. Click it again to reverse the order.
win98.help.live_tile_cancel_job: Click this to cancel the job on this tile.
win98.help.live_tile_commands: Shows the commands you can use on this tile. Only the commands that make sense for what is on the tile are shown.
win98.help.live_tile_delete_stockpile: Click this to delete the whole stockpile this tile belongs to. Its items stay where they are and are no longer kept there.
win98.help.live_tile_fell: Click this to mark the tree on this tile to be cut down, so a gnome will fell it for wood.
win98.help.live_tile_harvest: Click this to mark the plant on this tile for harvest, so a gnome will gather what it yields.
win98.help.live_tile_lower_job: Click this to lower the priority of the job on this tile, so gnomes do other work first.
win98.help.live_tile_manage: Click this to open the management window for the workshop, stockpile or farm on this tile.
win98.help.live_tile_mine: Click this to mark the tile for mining, so a gnome will dig it out.
win98.help.live_tile_open_creature: Click this to see the properties of the creature selected in the list.
win98.help.live_tile_raise_job: Click this to raise the priority of the job on this tile, so gnomes do it sooner.
win98.help.live_tile_remove_floor: Click this to mark the floor on this tile for removal, so a gnome will take it up.
win98.help.live_tile_remove_plant: Click this to mark the plant on this tile to be removed.
win98.help.live_tile_replace_floor: Click this to choose a new floor for this tile, then use Replace on the selected tile.
win98.help.live_tile_rows: Lists everything on the inspected tile, such as its wall, floor, plants, items, creatures, jobs and designation. Click a creature to select it, then click Inspect to see its properties.
win98.help.load-file-name: Shows the name of the save you selected in the list. This is the save that Open loads.
win98.help.load-kingdoms: Lists your kingdoms. Choose one to show its saves in the list below.
win98.help.load-saves: Lists the saves of the chosen kingdom, with the time each was made and the game version that made it. Click a save to select it, or double-click it to open it.
win98.help.load-selected: Click this to open the selected save and continue that kingdom. It is unavailable when no save is selected or the save was made by a version that cannot be opened.
win98.help.loading-retry: Click this to try preparing the kingdom again after it failed. It is unavailable when trying again cannot help.
win98.help.member_assign_squad: Click this to put the selected citizen into the squad chosen in the Squad box.
win98.help.member_move_to: Click this to move the selected citizen into the squad chosen in the Move to box.
win98.help.member_remove: Click this to take the selected citizen out of their squad. They then appear under Not in a squad.
win98.help.military_error_retry: Click this to try loading the military information again.
win98.help.military_member_destination: Selects another squad to move the selected citizen into. Click Move to make the change.
win98.help.military_member_role: Sets the role of the selected citizen. The role decides their uniform and whether they fight or retreat during an alarm; the change takes effect at once.
win98.help.military_member_rows: Lists the members of the chosen squad and the role of each. Click a member to change their role or move them.
win98.help.military_member_squad: Selects the squad whose members are shown on this page. Citizens you add go into this squad.
win98.help.military_priority_rows: Lists the kinds of creatures this squad may meet, in priority order, with the squad's response to each. Click a target to reorder it or change its response.
win98.help.military_priority_squad: Selects the squad whose targets are shown. Each squad has its own target order and responses.
win98.help.military_role_rows: Lists the roles and shows whether each is a combat or civilian role. Click a role to rename it, delete it or change it.
win98.help.military_squad_rows: Lists your squads. Click a squad to select it, so you can rename, move or delete it.
win98.help.military_tab_members: Shows the Members page, where you put citizens into squads and give them roles.
win98.help.military_tab_priorities: Shows the Targets page, where you choose which creatures each squad deals with first and how it responds to them.
win98.help.military_tab_roles: Shows the Roles page, where you create roles and mark whether they are for fighting or for civilians.
win98.help.military_tab_squads: Shows the Squads page, where you add, name, order and delete squads.
win98.help.military_tab_uniforms: Shows the Uniforms page, where you choose the equipment worn by citizens with each role.
win98.help.military_unassigned_rows: Lists citizens who are not in any squad. Select a citizen here, then click Add to put them in the chosen squad.
win98.help.military_uniform_material: Sets the material of the equipment in the selected slot. Only materials allowed for that equipment are offered.
win98.help.military_uniform_role: Selects the role whose uniform is shown. Uniform changes apply to every citizen with this role.
win98.help.military_uniform_rows: Lists the uniform slots of the chosen role, with the equipment and material for each. Click a slot to change it below.
win98.help.military_uniform_type: Sets the equipment worn in the selected slot. Only equipment that fits the slot is offered, and the change applies at once to everyone with this role.
win98.help.mission_action: Shows the task given to the emissary on this mission, or None for other kinds of mission.
win98.help.mission_action_ambassador: Has the emissary invite an ambassador from this kingdom.
win98.help.mission_action_improve: Has the emissary work to improve relations, which raises the kingdom's attitude toward your settlement.
win98.help.mission_action_insult: Has the emissary insult the kingdom, which lowers its attitude toward your settlement a good deal.
win98.help.mission_action_trader: Has the emissary invite a trader. If the mission succeeds, a trader from this kingdom comes to your settlement a few days later.
win98.help.mission_participants: Shows the citizens who went on this mission. They are away from the settlement until the mission returns.
win98.help.mission_result: Shows whether the mission succeeded. The result is known only after the citizens return.
win98.help.mission_start: Click this to send the mission as shown. The wizard closes and the Missions page shows the new mission.
win98.help.mission_step: Shows how far along this mission is, such as travelling or returned.
win98.help.mission_timing: Shows how many hours this mission has taken so far, or how long it took in total once it returned.
win98.help.mission_type_emissary: Sends an emissary with a diplomatic task you choose below. Spy, Raid and Sabotage are hostile missions; an emissary is the peaceful choice. Unavailable choices are not allowed by this kingdom.
win98.help.mission_type_raid: Sends a raid against this kingdom. Win or lose, a raid lowers the kingdom's attitude toward you.
win98.help.mission_type_sabotage: Sends a citizen to sabotage this kingdom. If it succeeds, their next raid on you is delayed by a few days, but their attitude toward you drops.
win98.help.mission_type_spy: Sends a spy to learn when this kingdom will raid you next. If the spy is caught, the kingdom's attitude toward you drops.
win98.help.mission_wizard_open: Click this to plan a mission to the selected kingdom. It is available only for a discovered kingdom that allows at least one kind of mission.
win98.help.neighbor_attitude: Shows how this kingdom feels about your settlement. Emissaries sent to improve relations raise it; insults, raids, sabotage and failed spying lower it.
win98.help.neighbor_distance: Shows how far away this kingdom is. Citizens sent on a mission must travel there and back, so distant kingdoms take longer.
win98.help.neighbor_economy: Shows what this kingdom's economy is like.
win98.help.neighbor_military: Shows how strong this kingdom's military is. Check it before you decide to raid or sabotage the kingdom.
win98.help.neighbor_type: Shows what kind of kingdom this is.
win98.help.neighbor_wealth: Shows how wealthy this kingdom is.
win98.help.new-back: Click this to return to the previous page of the wizard. Your choices are kept.
win98.help.new-flatness: Sets how much the height of the land varies. At 0 the surface is level; higher values make the hills and valleys taller and deeper.
win98.help.new-flatness-exact: Sets how much the height of the land varies. At 0 the surface is level; higher values make the hills and valleys taller and deeper.
win98.help.new-gnomes: Sets how many gnomes start in your settlement. More settlers get early work done faster but also need more food and shelter.
win98.help.new-gnomes-exact: Sets how many gnomes start in your settlement. More settlers get early work done faster but also need more food and shelter.
win98.help.new-ground: Sets the level where the surface lies. Everything below it is underground rock, so a higher ground level leaves more room to dig down.
win98.help.new-ground-exact: Sets the level where the surface lies. Everything below it is underground rock, so a higher ground level leaves more room to dig down.
win98.help.new-kingdom-name: Sets the name of your new kingdom. The name identifies the kingdom later when you load its saves.
win98.help.new-next: Click this to go to the next page of the wizard. If a number on this page is out of range, you stay on the page so you can correct it.
win98.help.new-ocean-size: Sets how much ocean lies along one edge of the map. At 0 there is no ocean.
win98.help.new-ocean-size-exact: Sets how much ocean lies along one edge of the map. At 0 there is no ocean.
win98.help.new-peaceful: Turns off raids and invasions by neighboring kingdoms. Select it if you want to build without having to defend your settlement.
win98.help.new-plant-density: Sets how much of the land is covered with plants and bushes. At 0 there are none.
win98.help.new-plant-density-exact: Sets how much of the land is covered with plants and bushes. At 0 there are none.
win98.help.new-random-name: Click this to replace the kingdom name with a randomly chosen one.
win98.help.new-random-seed: Click this to replace the seed with a random one, so the new world is different from the last.
win98.help.new-river-size: Sets how many tiles wide each river is. At 0 the rivers are as narrow as they can be.
win98.help.new-river-size-exact: Sets how many tiles wide each river is. At 0 the rivers are as narrow as they can be.
win98.help.new-rivers: Sets how many rivers cross the world. Rivers bring water close to your settlement; at 0 there are none.
win98.help.new-rivers-exact: Sets how many rivers cross the world. Rivers bring water close to your settlement; at 0 there are none.
win98.help.new-seed: Sets the seed the world is built from. Using the same seed with the same settings lets you create the same world again.
win98.help.new-start: Click this to create the world and start the new kingdom with the settings shown. It is unavailable while any setting is out of range.
win98.help.new-start-zone: Sets how many tiles from the center of the map are kept free of trees, plants and wild animals, giving your settlers open ground to start on.
win98.help.new-start-zone-exact: Sets how many tiles from the center of the map are kept free of trees, plants and wild animals, giving your settlers open ground to start on.
win98.help.new-tree-density: Sets how much of the land is covered with trees. Trees are your main source of wood; at 0 there are none.
win98.help.new-tree-density-exact: Sets how much of the land is covered with trees. Trees are your main source of wood; at 0 there are none.
win98.help.new-wild-animals: Sets how many wild animals live in the world when it is created. Animals can be hunted, but some of them are dangerous.
win98.help.new-wild-animals-exact: Sets how many wild animals live in the world when it is created. Animals can be hunted, but some of them are dangerous.
win98.help.new-world-size: Sets how many tiles wide the world is. A larger world gives you more room and resources to explore, but takes longer to create.
win98.help.new-world-size-exact: Sets how many tiles wide the world is. A larger world gives you more room and resources to explore, but takes longer to create.
win98.help.new-z-levels: Sets how many levels high the world is, from its deepest rock to its sky. More levels give you more depth to dig into.
win98.help.new-z-levels-exact: Sets how many levels high the world is, from its deepest rock to its sky. More levels give you more depth to dig into.
win98.help.pause-load: Click this to leave this kingdom and choose another save to open. You are asked to confirm first.
win98.help.pause-menu: Click this to leave this kingdom and return to the main menu. You are asked to confirm first.
win98.help.pause-resume: Click this to close this box and let time run again in your kingdom.
win98.help.pause-save: Click this to save your kingdom now, so you can return to this point later. The result is shown at the top of the box.
win98.help.pause-settings: Click this to change display, controls, sound and autosave settings without leaving the game.
win98.help.population_open_citizen: Click this to open the details of the selected citizen, where you can review their needs, skills and equipment.
win98.help.population_refresh: Click this to reload the citizen information from the game, so the list shows the latest names and professions.
win98.help.population_rows: Lists your citizens and their professions. Click a citizen to select them, or double-click to open their details.
win98.help.population_search: Shows only citizens whose name or profession contains the text you type. Clear the box to see everyone again.
win98.help.population_sort_name: Sorts the citizen list by name. Click it again to reverse the order.
win98.help.population_sort_profession: Sorts the citizen list by profession, so citizens with the same job are grouped together. Click it again to reverse the order.
win98.help.population_tab_citizens: Shows the Citizens page, which lists every citizen and their profession. Use it to find a citizen and open their details.
win98.help.population_tab_professions: Shows the Professions page, where you create professions and choose the skills each one uses, in priority order.
win98.help.population_tab_schedules: Shows the Schedules page, a grid of 24 hours for each citizen. Use it to plan when citizens eat, sleep and train.
win98.help.population_tab_skills: Shows the Skills page, where you choose a skill and decide which citizens may do that kind of work.
win98.help.priority_move_down: Click this to lower the selected target's priority, so the squad deals with other targets first.
win98.help.priority_move_up: Click this to raise the selected target's priority, so the squad deals with it before targets lower in the list.
win98.help.profession_available_skills: Lists the skills the selected profession does not use yet. Select a skill here, then click Add to give it to the profession.
win98.help.profession_create: Click this to add a new profession named New Profession and select it, so you can rename it and choose its skills.
win98.help.profession_delete: Click this to delete the selected profession and its skill list. You are asked to confirm, and you cannot undo it. The base Gnomad profession cannot be deleted.
win98.help.profession_discard: Click this to throw away your unsaved changes and show the profession as it is now saved.
win98.help.profession_name: Sets the name of the selected profession. The new name is used after you click Save Changes.
win98.help.profession_rows: Selects the profession to view or edit. If you have unsaved changes, you are asked whether to save them first.
win98.help.profession_save: Click this to save your changes to the profession's name and skills. Until you save, the game keeps the old settings.
win98.help.profession_selected_skills: Lists the skills this profession uses, highest priority first. Citizens with this profession look for work in this order.
win98.help.profession_skill_add: Click this to add the skill selected under Available skills to the profession. It goes to the end of the list, so it has the lowest priority.
win98.help.profession_skill_down: Click this to give the selected skill a lower priority, so citizens with this profession choose that work later.
win98.help.profession_skill_remove: Click this to take the selected skill out of the profession. Citizens with this profession will no longer do that work.
win98.help.profession_skill_up: Click this to give the selected skill a higher priority, so citizens with this profession choose that work sooner.
win98.help.review_citizen: Shows the citizen you chose to send on this mission.
win98.help.review_destination: Shows the kingdom this mission will go to.
win98.help.review_mission: Shows the kind of mission you chose, and the emissary's task if there is one.
win98.help.role_add: Click this to add a new role. Then name it and set its uniform on the Uniforms page.
win98.help.role_civilian: Marks the selected role as civilian. Citizens with a civilian role retreat to safety during an alarm instead of fighting.
win98.help.role_name_input: Shows the name of the selected role. Type a new name, then click Rename.
win98.help.role_remove: Click this to delete the selected role. You are asked to confirm first.
win98.help.role_rename: Click this to give the selected role the name typed in the Name box.
win98.help.schedule_apply: Click this to give the selected cells the activity chosen above. If more than one citizen is selected, you are asked to confirm first.
win98.help.schedule_grid: Shows each citizen's day, one row per citizen and one column per hour. Letters show the activity: E eat, S sleep, T train; a blank cell has none.
win98.help.schedule_hours: Shows the hours of the day. Click an hour to select that hour for all citizens, for example to give everyone the same meal time.
win98.help.schedule_names: Shows the citizens in the grid. Click a name to select all 24 hours of that citizen's day.
win98.help.schedule_rows: Shows the activity planned for each citizen and hour. Click a cell to select it, or Shift+click to select a range of cells, then click Set Activity.
win98.help.schedule_select_all: Click this to select every hour for every citizen, so Set Activity changes the whole grid.
win98.help.schedule_set_eat: Chooses Eat for the selected hours, shown as E in the grid. Choosing an option does not change the grid until you click Set Activity.
win98.help.schedule_set_none: Chooses no activity for the selected hours, which clears them. Eat, Sleep and Train set a fixed activity instead. Choosing an option does not change the grid until you click Set Activity.
win98.help.schedule_set_sleep: Chooses Sleep for the selected hours, shown as S in the grid. Choosing an option does not change the grid until you click Set Activity.
win98.help.schedule_set_training: Chooses Train for the selected hours, shown as T in the grid, so citizens practice then. Choosing an option does not change the grid until you click Set Activity.
win98.help.selection_rotate: Click this to rotate the object you are placing before you put it down.
win98.help.setting-autosave-continue: Keeps the game running after an automatic save. Clear it if you want the game to stay paused after each autosave.
win98.help.setting-autosave-interval: Sets how many game days pass between automatic saves. Shorter intervals lose less progress if something goes wrong.
win98.help.setting-follow-refresh: Limits the frame rate to your monitor's refresh rate. Clear it to set your own limit with Frame rate limit.
win98.help.setting-frame-rate: Sets the highest number of frames the game draws each second. A lower limit uses less power and keeps your computer cooler. It is unavailable while Match the monitor refresh rate is selected.
win98.help.setting-fullscreen: Fills the whole screen with the game. Clear it to play in a window instead.
win98.help.setting-keyboard-speed: Sets how fast the view moves when you pan the camera with the keyboard.
win98.help.setting-master-volume: Sets the loudness of all game sound.
win98.help.setting-minimum-light: Sets how bright the darkest places on the map are drawn. Raise it if tunnels and nights are too dark to see what your gnomes are doing.
win98.help.setting-ui-scale: Sets the size of the windows, text and buttons. Make it larger if the text is hard to read, or smaller to see more of the map.
win98.help.setting-wheel-level: Chooses whether turning the mouse wheel over the map changes the level you are viewing or zooms the view in and out. Change it if the wheel does the opposite of what you expect.
win98.help.settings-reset: Click this to return every setting on all pages to its recommended value. The change takes effect at once.
win98.help.settings-tab-controls: Shows the settings for moving the camera and for the mouse wheel.
win98.help.settings-tab-display: Shows the settings for the screen, the interface size and the minimum light on the map.
win98.help.settings-tab-saving: Shows the settings for automatic saving.
win98.help.settings-tab-sound: Shows the setting for the game volume.
win98.help.shell-continue: Click this to open your most recent save that this version can load, so you can pick up where you left off. It is unavailable when no compatible save is found.
win98.help.shell-exit: Click this to close Ingnomia. You are asked to confirm first.
win98.help.shell-load: Click this to choose a kingdom and one of its saves to open. Use it to return to an older save or a different kingdom.
win98.help.shell-new-default: Starts a new kingdom right away with the recommended world and settlement settings. Use it when you want to play without choosing any settings first.
win98.help.shell-new-setup: Opens a wizard where you choose the world size, terrain, wildlife and your starting settlement before the new kingdom is created.
win98.help.shell-settings: Click this to change display, interface, camera, sound and autosave settings. Changes take effect at once.
win98.help.shell-tutorial: Starts a guided first settlement that teaches the basics step by step: gathering, digging, storing, crafting, farming and shelter. Use it if you are new to Ingnomia.
win98.help.skill_citizen_rows: Lists the citizens who have the selected skill and their level in it. Check a citizen to let them do this work, or clear the check to stop them; the change takes effect at once.
win98.help.skill_disable_all: Click this to stop every citizen from using the selected skill, for example to keep them all on other work. You are asked to confirm first.
win98.help.skill_enable_all: Click this to let every citizen who has the selected skill use it. You are asked to confirm first, because this also changes citizens hidden by the Find text.
win98.help.skills_catalog_rows: Lists every skill in the game. Click a skill to see which citizens have it and whether they may use it.
win98.help.squad_add: Click this to add a new squad. Then use the Name box to give it a name you will recognize.
win98.help.squad_move_down: Click this to move the selected squad down in the list. This changes only the order of the list.
win98.help.squad_move_up: Click this to move the selected squad up in the list. This changes only the order of the list.
win98.help.squad_name_input: Shows the name of the selected squad. Type a new name, then click Rename.
win98.help.squad_remove: Click this to delete the selected squad. You are asked to confirm first.
win98.help.squad_rename: Click this to give the selected squad the name typed in the Name box.
win98.help.stockpile_allow_bulk: Click this to check every item now shown in the list, so the stockpile accepts them all. Use Find or Category first to limit which items change.
win98.help.stockpile_allow_category: Filters the list to one category of items. The same category also filters the Contents page.
win98.help.stockpile_allow_pull: Shows whether higher-priority stockpiles may take items from this one.
win98.help.stockpile_allow_search: Filters the Items this stockpile accepts list to items whose names contain the text you type.
win98.help.stockpile_allow_sort_group: Click this to sort the list by item type. Click again to reverse the order.
win98.help.stockpile_allow_sort_item: Click this to sort the list by item name. Click again to reverse the order.
win98.help.stockpile_allow_sort_material: Click this to sort the list by material. Click again to reverse the order.
win98.help.stockpile_block_bulk: Click this to clear every item now shown in the list, so the stockpile accepts none of them. Use Find or Category first to limit which items change.
win98.help.stockpile_capacity: Shows how many items are stored here and how many the stockpile can hold.
win98.help.stockpile_content_category: Filters the list to one category of items. The same category also filters the Allow List page.
win98.help.stockpile_content_search: Filters the Items stored here list to items whose names contain the text you type.
win98.help.stockpile_content_sort_item: Click this to sort the list by item name. Click again to reverse the order.
win98.help.stockpile_content_sort_materi: Click this to sort the list by material. Click again to reverse the order.
win98.help.stockpile_content_sort_stock: Click this to sort the list by the number stored in this stockpile. Click again to reverse the order.
win98.help.stockpile_content_sort_total: Click this to sort the list by the total number of that item stored in all stockpiles. Click again to reverse the order.
win98.help.stockpile_contents: Lists the items stored in this stockpile, with each item's material and quantity.
win98.help.stockpile_filters: Lists every item and material. Check an item to let gnomes haul it into this stockpile, or clear it to keep it out. Changes take effect when you click Apply or OK.
win98.help.stockpile_locate: Click this to center the map view on this stockpile.
win98.help.stockpile_name: Sets the name of this stockpile. A clear name helps you find it later. The change takes effect when you click Apply or OK.
win98.help.stockpile_priority: Sets this stockpile's priority; 1 is the highest. Higher-priority stockpiles are filled first. The change takes effect when you click Apply or OK.
win98.help.stockpile_pull_from_others: Shows whether this stockpile takes items from lower-priority stockpiles.
win98.help.stockpile_reserved: Shows how many stored items are already claimed for a job or for hauling.
win98.help.stockpile_rows: Lists the items stored here, with how many are in this stockpile and in total. Click an item to find it on the Allow List page.
win98.help.stockpile_status: Shows whether the stockpile is accepting items or suspended.
win98.help.stockpile_template_load: Click this to replace this stockpile's allow list with the named template. You are asked to confirm first.
win98.help.stockpile_template_name: Names this allow list so you can save it as a template, or chooses a saved template to load. Templates let you set up new stockpiles quickly.
win98.help.stockpile_template_options: Lists your saved allow list templates. Click one to put its name in the Template box.
win98.help.stockpile_template_save: Click this to save this stockpile's allow list as a template under the typed name. If the name already exists, you are asked before it is replaced.
win98.help.stockpile_template_toggle: Click this to show the saved templates and choose one.
win98.help.stockpile_toggle_allow_pull: Lets higher-priority stockpiles take items out of this one.
win98.help.stockpile_toggle_pull: Lets gnomes move accepted items from lower-priority stockpiles into this one, so your most important stockpile stays full.
win98.help.stockpile_toggle_suspended: Stops gnomes from bringing items to this stockpile while checked. Items already stored stay here.
win98.help.stockpile_view_allow: Shows the Allow List page, where you choose which items this stockpile accepts.
win98.help.stockpile_view_contents: Shows the Contents page, which lists the items stored in this stockpile.
win98.help.stockpile_view_settings: Shows the General page, where you rename the stockpile, set its priority and choose how hauling works.
win98.help.tile_cancel_job: Click this to cancel the job on this tile.
win98.help.tile_delete_stockpile: Click this to delete the whole stockpile this tile belongs to. Its items stay where they are and are no longer kept there.
win98.help.tile_fell: Click this to mark the tree on this tile to be cut down, so a gnome will fell it for wood.
win98.help.tile_harvest: Click this to mark the plant on this tile for harvest, so a gnome will gather what it yields.
win98.help.tile_lower_job: Click this to lower the priority of the job on this tile, so gnomes do other work first.
win98.help.tile_manage: Click this to open the management window for the workshop, stockpile or farm on this tile.
win98.help.tile_mine: Click this to mark the tile for mining, so a gnome will dig it out.
win98.help.tile_open_creature: Click this to see the properties of the creature selected in the list.
win98.help.tile_raise_job: Click this to raise the priority of the job on this tile, so gnomes do it sooner.
win98.help.tile_remove_floor: Click this to mark the floor on this tile for removal, so a gnome will take it up.
win98.help.tile_remove_plant: Click this to mark the plant on this tile to be removed.
win98.help.tile_replace_floor: Click this to choose a new floor for this tile, then use Replace on the selected tile.
win98.help.tutorial-continue: Click this to go on to the next lesson. It appears when the current lesson is done or skipped.
win98.help.tutorial-finish: Click this to end the tutorial. It appears on the last lesson.
win98.help.tutorial-hints: Shows or hides the lesson's explanation, its steps and the highlighting of the controls to use. Hide hints if you want to try the lesson on your own.
win98.help.tutorial-restart: Click this to start the tutorial again from the first lesson.
win98.help.tutorial-skip: Click this to skip the current lesson. Skipped lessons are marked in the lesson list.
win98.help.tutorial_checklist: Lists all the tutorial lessons. A check mark means the lesson is done; the current and skipped lessons are marked.
win98.help.tutorial_steps: Shows the steps of the current lesson. A check mark means you have done that step.
win98.help.wizard_back: Click this to go back to the previous page so you can change your choices.
win98.help.wizard_next: Click this to go to the next page. It becomes available once you have made a choice on this page.
win98.help.workshop_auto: Shows whether the workshop crafts missing components on its own when a job needs them. Change it in the workshop's management window.
win98.help.workshop_generated: Shows whether this workshop accepts craft orders the game creates on its own. Change it in the workshop's management window.
win98.help.workshop_job_apply: Click this to save the Type, Quantity and move-to-bottom choices you changed for the selected order.
win98.help.workshop_job_bottom: Click this to move the selected order to the bottom of the queue, behind every other order.
win98.help.workshop_job_cancel: Click this to remove the selected order from the queue.
win98.help.workshop_job_count: Sets the quantity or stock limit for the selected order. The change takes effect when you click Update Order.
win98.help.workshop_job_down: Click this to move the selected order one place lower, so other orders are worked on first.
win98.help.workshop_job_mode: Sets how the selected order runs: Craft number, Stock limit or Repeat. The change takes effect when you click Update Order.
win98.help.workshop_job_move_back: Sends the selected order to the bottom of the queue each time it finishes an item, so the workshop takes turns between orders. The change takes effect when you click Update Order.
win98.help.workshop_job_suspend: Click this to pause the selected order, or to resume it if it is paused. A paused order stays in the queue but is not worked on.
win98.help.workshop_job_top: Click this to move the selected order to the top of the queue, so it is worked on next.
win98.help.workshop_job_up: Click this to move the selected order one place higher, so it is worked on sooner.
win98.help.workshop_link: Shows whether the workshop collects its materials from linked stockpiles first.
win98.help.workshop_linked_stockpiles: Lists your stockpiles. Check the ones this workshop should collect materials from first; the nearest checked stockpile is used first, then any other stockpile.
win98.help.workshop_locate: Click this to center the map view on this workshop.
win98.help.workshop_name: Sets the name of this workshop. A clear name helps you find it later. The change takes effect when you click Apply or OK.
win98.help.workshop_order_count: Sets how many items to craft, or for a Stock limit order, the stock to keep on hand. It is not used for Repeat orders.
win98.help.workshop_order_mode: Sets how the new order runs. Craft number makes a set amount and stops, Stock limit crafts until your stock reaches the limit, and Repeat crafts until you suspend or cancel it.
win98.help.workshop_priority: Sets this workshop's place in the order the game serves workshops; 1 comes first. The change takes effect when you click Apply or OK.
win98.help.workshop_product_selection: Shows the materials the selected craft needs. Use each list to choose which material to use for that component; the number in stock is shown next to each choice.
win98.help.workshop_products: Lists the crafts this workshop can make. Click a craft to set up a new order for it on the right.
win98.help.workshop_queue: Lists this workshop's orders; workers take them from top to bottom. Click an order to change, move, suspend or cancel it.
win98.help.workshop_queue_once: Click this to add the new order to the end of this workshop's queue. If materials are short, the order waits until they are in stock.
win98.help.workshop_queued: Shows how many jobs are waiting in this workshop's queue.
win98.help.workshop_search: Filters the Available crafts list to crafts whose names contain the text you type. Clear the box to see every craft again.
win98.help.workshop_state: Shows whether the workshop is working or suspended. A suspended workshop takes no new jobs.
win98.help.workshop_toggle_auto_missing: Asks workshops that accept generated orders to make any missing component that can be crafted, so you do not have to order it yourself.
win98.help.workshop_toggle_catch: Sets whether workers at this fishery go fishing.
win98.help.workshop_toggle_corpses: Sets whether this butcher's shop processes animal corpses.
win98.help.workshop_toggle_excess: Lets this butcher's shop butcher tame adult animals that are not assigned to any pasture. Use it to keep your animal numbers down.
win98.help.workshop_toggle_generated: Lets this workshop receive orders the game creates on its own when something needs a craftable item that is not in stock.
win98.help.workshop_toggle_process: Sets whether workers at this fishery process caught fish.
win98.help.workshop_toggle_suspended: Stops all work at this workshop while checked. Orders stay in the queue and continue when you clear the check box.
win98.help.workshop_trade_count: Sets how many of the selected item to include in the trade, from 0 up to the amount available. Click Set Offer to use it.
win98.help.workshop_trade_execute: Click this to review the trade before it happens. It is available only when you have offered goods worth at least as much as the goods you receive.
win98.help.workshop_trade_merchant: Lists the goods the merchant has for sale, with the amount available, how many you have offered to take and the value of each. Click an item to set how many you want.
win98.help.workshop_trade_refresh: Click this to reload both lists of goods so they show the current stock.
win98.help.workshop_trade_set: Click this to put the amount in the Offer box into the trade for the selected item. The totals below update to show the new balance.
win98.help.workshop_trade_settlement: Lists the goods your settlement can trade, with the amount available, how many you have offered to give and the value of each. Click an item to set how many to give.
win98.help.workshop_view_craft: Shows the Craft page, where you choose something this workshop can make and add an order for it.
win98.help.workshop_view_queue: Shows the Queue page, which lists this workshop's orders. The number on the tab is how many orders are waiting.
win98.help.workshop_view_settings: Shows the General page, where you rename the workshop, set its priority and choose how it works.
win98.help.workshop_view_stockpiles: Shows the Stockpiles page, where you choose which stockpiles this workshop collects its materials from first.
win98.help.workshop_view_trade: Shows the Trade page, where you exchange goods with a visiting merchant.
